lessons: cycles 1-7 (retrospective, added with the strategy upgrade): The CAT round-trip validated evidence-based decisions both ways - cycle 5 correctly held CAT through a -5% dip when research showed strength (dividend raise, target hikes), and cycle 7 correctly exited when research showed real deterioration (margin compression, tariff guide, downgrade). cycle 12: LIN's fundamentals kept strengthening while the stock stayed below its 50-day SMA — price-vs-SMA and business-quality are genuinely separate signals; requiring both (not overriding a weak trend score because the business is good) is the actual edge.

cycles 1-12 (owner review 2026-08-14, the big one): The portfolio drifted into CLOSET INDEXING and nobody noticed because the returns looked fine. 17 positions, 6 of them ETFs that largely duplicated VOO and each other, 11 single names all already inside VOO, 14% idle cash — ~39% of the account expressing no view. Return: +2.81% vs SPY +2.89%. The cause was a self-contradicting brief: 'maximize long-term profit' paired with rules that mandate becoming the index. Lesson: diversification rules and a profit-maximizing mandate pull in opposite directions, and when they conflict the rules win silently. Every dollar must express a view.

cycles 10-12 (owner review 2026-08-14): The four-cycle no-trade stretch was misdiagnosed as an over-strict scoring bar. The actual failure was a FUNNEL of only three stale candidates (LIN/AMT/CAT) re-checked cycle after cycle, with zero new names screened. Lesson: when nothing passes the bar, screen more candidates; never lower the bar.

cycle 13: A restructure that sells several positions in one cash-account cycle runs into T+1 settlement — sale proceeds are not spendable same-day. Plan buy sequencing around settled buying power, not gross cash, and don't be surprised when 'cash %' looks high right after a big sell day; check buying_power specifically, not just the cash field, before sizing buys.

cycle 13: The most durable candidates on a multi-cycle watchlist (AMT, 13 cycles of 'not yet') can still eventually clear the technical bar — AMT's SMA breakout this cycle is a reminder not to drop a name just because it's been patient; the discipline of waiting for a real signal instead of a stale re-check was the point of keeping it on the list at all.
